| Lab | POST lab-orders; GET lab-orders; POST specimens/{id}/transitions | Assigned lab/mode and bounded worklists |
| Reports | POST report-drafts; POST reports/{id}/release or amendments | Reviewer capability, checksum/version, private access |
| Billing | POST invoices; POST receipts; POST credits; POST payment-intents/refunds | Distinct financial states; merchant/issuer validation |
| Files | POST documents/upload-grants; POST documents/{id}/complete; POST access-grants | Allowed size/type/owner, quarantine, short-lived access |
| Vendor/operations | GET assignments/statements/jobs; POST deliveries/{id}/replay | Permitted fields, visible processing state and audited recovery |
| Incoming integrations | POST /api/v2/integrations/{integrationId}/webhooks | Provider authentication, raw bytes if required, durable inbox |
| Public discovery | GET approved branches/services/tariffs | Explicit public projection; no private-catalogue or patient leakage |

Patient-facing routes are distinct from organization-member administration:

| Proposed patient surface | Authorization / contract |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/v2/me/patients | Only verified own/represented identities, with representative scope/expiry |
| GET /api/v2/me/patients/{patientId}/appointments or reports | Aggregate permitted records across businesses; constrain each owning business, release policy and purpose |
| GET /api/v2/me/invoices or payments | Payer/customer rights; paying another patient's bill does not grant their clinical chart |
| POST /api/v2/me/appointments or orders | Patient relationship plus valid service offer/branch/quote; server derives business, price and permitted public/invited access |
| POST /api/v2/me/appointments/{id}/cancel or documents/{id}/access-grants | Verify linked patient, resource owner, representative scope and state; no business membership assumption |

List APIs use bounded page size (proposal default 25/max 100), stable cursor sort and authorized filters. Mutations return 200/201 only for the defined local result; 202 means durable processing, with `operationId` and a status URL, not completed provider fulfilment. Errors include stable code, safe message, correlation ID and retryability: 401 unauthenticated,403 denied,404 absent/hidden according to policy,409 state/idempotency/capacity conflict,422 domain validation,429 throttled,503 unavailable dependency/acceptance store. Never expose raw provider payloads or stack traces.

Example **proposed** asynchronous response:

```json
{
  "operationId": "op_demo_001",
  "status": "processing",
  "resourceId": "order_demo_001",
  "statusUrl": "/api/v2/operations/op_demo_001",
  "correlationId": "req_demo_001"
}
```

**AR-26 command-specific writable fields.** Every current/v2 command validates an explicit actor-specific allow-list and rechecks service-level authority. Generic create/update bodies cannot set balances/initialBalance, ledger effects, payment/collection states, fulfilment counters, verified/active privilege flags, ratings, corporate/tenant ownership, shared catalogue restrictions or clinician-authored/finalized evidence. Derive those from verified actor/resource/payment facts and dedicated authorized commands with version, idempotency and audit. Legitimate uploaded prescriptions remain unverified imported material; they are not clinician-authored records merely because they arrived in a booking body. Approved private tariff changes are separate from payment-state/verification authority. Forbidden fields return422 only after object/action authorization; unauthenticated/unauthorized requests receive401/403 or the approved hidden-object404. Legacy clients receive explicit migration/error behavior; never silently accept or drop an authority-changing field. Apply this boundary to existing v1 routes in M0, not only future v2 schemas. Withdraw raw caller-chosen OTP creation from public access while retaining legitimate rate-limited server-generated login challenge requests. Sensitive authentication mail has no unapproved CC/BCC recipients; notification broadcast/test-push and privileged recovery tools require explicit capability and scoped targets.

A reused idempotency key and body returns the stored authorized result/reference; incompatible body returns 409. PATCH-like state changes require expected version/If-Match. Legacy clients receive mapped states and equivalent errors through a compatibility adapter; do not change existing numeric amount units or report URL behavior without a versioned migration and deadline. Define OpenAPI schemas/provider fixtures before implementation; this document is not the generated API specification.

## 11. Events, inbox/outbox and worker contracts

Internal durable events/inbox/outbox are required. An external outbound subscription/webhook platform is conditional on a named approved subscriber and signed delivery contract; M4/M5 schedules that adapter only when selected. Do not make every lab install an external subscriber or build the entire optional platform in M0. Initial delivery uses Mongo-backed durable records. Harden the current queue or replace it only after the [open source trial](OPEN_SOURCE_OPTIONS.md). BullMQ is conditional; current source describes Redis and optional PostgreSQL, but exact published version/backend compatibility needs proof. The outbox contract remains independent of that choice.

```json
{
  "eventId": "evt_demo_001",
  "eventType": "lab.report.released",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "organizationId": "org_demo_001",
  "resourceType": "labReport",
  "resourceId": "report_demo_001",
  "resourceVersion": 2,
  "occurredAt": "2026-11-08T10:00:00Z",
  "correlationId": "req_demo_001",
  "causationId": "cmd_demo_001",
  "payload": {
    "labOrderId": "laborder_demo_001",
    "documentId": "doc_demo_001"
  }
}
```

Events carry minimal IDs/facts, not entire patient charts, access tokens, report contents or secrets. Authorization governs recipient projection; a publisher's business scope is not permission for every subscriber. Schema version is different from resource version. Additive compatible changes retain schema; breaking changes require a new version and tested consumer transition.

| Mechanism | Durable contract | Recovery rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outbox | Written with domain change; immutable event plus delivery state | Dispatcher claims due work by compare-and-set lease, publishes, then records attempt/outcome |
| Internal consumer | Unique consumer/event receipt, expected resource version | Commit local effect plus processed marker together; duplicate delivery is harmless |
| Incoming status/domain inbox | Authenticate first, unique integration/event identity, hash/provenance, bounded protected payload; PIN input is excluded | Acknowledge only after durable write; duplicates acknowledge without repeating effects; store unavailable -> retryable non-2xx |
| PIN verification receipt | Authenticate bounded input transiently; retain only safe session/attempt reference and non-secret outcome | Section8.5 and phone3.1 exception: no raw digits or unkeyed PIN-derived payload digest in any queue/archive; any retained envelope hash covers sanitized fields only |
| External command | Original business/provider reference, payload hash, attempt/unknown outcome | Lookup/reconcile before non-idempotent retry; escalating unknown is safer than a duplicate charge/booking |
| Optional outgoing webhook, only after subscriber gate | Subscription/tenant scope, filtered body, event ID, secret version, attempt state | Signed delivery, exponential backoff/jitter, terminal recovery queue and audited replay |
| Scheduler | Unique task/business/time-window key and lease/fencing token | Only current lease owner enqueues; repeated ticks cannot duplicate the business effect |

Lease duration must exceed normal task time and renew during long work. A monotonically increasing fencing token guards ownership writes; expired workers cannot overwrite newer state. External calls may still duplicate around a crash, so provider/consumer idempotency and reconciliation remain essential. Bound attempts, execution time, body size and concurrency per provider/business; retries stop on permanent validation errors and enter visible recovery. Redact secrets and minimize protected payload retention.

Delivery is **at least once**, with idempotent local effects. Marking an event delivered before sending loses work; sending then crashing may duplicate it. A repeated provider event ID with a different payload hash is a conflict requiring protected evidence/reconciliation, not an overwrite. No global ordering is assumed. Resource sequence/version and allowed transition checks reject stale state; gaps trigger fetch/reconciliation rather than inventing missing clinical stages. Queue age, due-task age and recovery count are operational metrics, not hidden logs.

Proposed initial event set: appointment held/confirmed/cancelled; order reserved/dispensed/returned; stock received/transferred/consumed/adjusted; encounter finalized/amended; prescription issued/amended; lab report released/amended; collection recorded; refund confirmed; settlement confirmed; care task due/completed. Every owner defines its specific effect keys, payload and recipients before shipping; this list is not a generic event-sourcing mandate. Current state remains in domain records, with immutable movements/journals/audit for their purposes.

## 12. Provider ports, webhooks and clinical documents

A lab provider adapter exposes explicit capabilities: catalog/tariff mapping, create-order, get-order, cancel if supported, report retrieval and incoming-event verification. It returns provider IDs, known/unknown state and evidence, never a falsely universal success response. Partners without APIs use the same domain commands via scoped panel actions. Calendar/video/message providers have independent timeout, quota and retry policy; one outage does not block unrelated counter billing.

Webhook verification is provider-specific. Razorpay verification uses raw request bytes and the configured webhook secret; checkout signature verification is a different contract. Register the exact raw-body webhook route before the existing global `express.json()` parser in `src1/index.ts`, handle secret versions for retries, deduplicate provider event IDs and validate business facts. Razorpay also documents duplicate and out-of-order delivery. [Official verification guide](https://razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/validate-test/). For a lab with no documented signing scheme, establish supported authentication or use authenticated polling; never invent an HMAC contract the vendor does not implement.

When the named-subscriber gate is met, outbound subscriptions use HTTPS, rotated per-subscriber secrets, event/timestamp/body signatures, replay windows and immutable delivery IDs. Validate host/IP destinations at registration and delivery, restrict private/loopback/link-local/metadata networks, control DNS resolution/redirects and enforce outbound network policy. Apply similar protection to report-import URLs; limit bytes and MIME/content. [OWASP SSRF guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html).

Document lifecycle: declared -> uploading -> quarantined -> validated -> approved/released, with rejected/superseded branches. Authorize declared owner/patient/order before granting upload. Use unpredictable object keys, allowlisted formats, checksum/size checks, malware scanning and actual file-type inspection. Upload success alone does not establish report approval or a valid prescription. Completion verifies stored object/version/checksum and moves metadata only through authorized transitions. Remove abandoned uploads through separate retention cleanup.

Clinical reads pass through an authorized document gateway so revocation and access audit are evaluated on each request. The gateway streams from private object storage without synchronous whole-file disk reads. Short-lived direct grants may be used only for approved lower-risk cases with explicit revocation limits and scope; do not promise immediate revocation of an already issued bearer URL. Keep no public clinical bucket, long-lived `/api/static/*` report link or public-cache response. Clinical access responses use appropriate private/no-store controls; retention and legal holds cover both metadata and object versions.

Third-party report fetching happens in workers with restricted egress; readers receive a validated private artifact, not an unrestricted proxy to a user-supplied URL. Corrected reports retain version/provenance and clinician notification/review consequences. Restore verification checks object hashes and links, not just database row counts.

## 13. Deployment and operating model

Proposed initial topology is provider-neutral and sized by measurement. Container/orchestrated deployment configuration is implementation work; none is implied to exist in this checkout.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  U[Apps and business panels] --> L[TLS edge, limits and routing]
  L --> A[Two stateless API replicas]
  A --> D[(Private MongoDB replica set)]
  A --> F[Authorized gateway to private object storage]
  D --> W[Separate worker pool and leased scheduler]
  W --> F
  W --> E[Restricted egress to external providers]
  W -. optional after trial .-> Q[Selected ERP, LIS or queue store]
  A --> O[Metrics, traces and redacted logs]
  W --> O
```

Start benchmarking with two API replicas and a separate bounded worker deployment, each roughly 2 vCPU/4 GiB as an experiment; not a production capacity promise. Use a correctly operated Mongo replica set/managed equivalent with failure-domain separation, private networking, backups and measured IOPS/memory. Avoid placing every component on one host and calling it high availability. No Kubernetes, Kafka, Redis, SQL ERP or service mesh is mandatory merely for 100 RPS.

API serves local commands/queries; worker handles reports/PDFs, imports, integrations, notifications, reconciliation and outbox. Scheduler is a separately leased execution role; it may share a worker binary, never duplicate tasks per API replica. Assign per-class concurrency so bulk imports cannot starve payment/report work. Shared process image is acceptable with explicit runtime role; public API credentials must not automatically authorize all back-office operations.

Define process liveness, dependency readiness and worker readiness separately. DB outage makes durable-write APIs unavailable; provider outage leaves only affected capabilities degraded. A report scanner outage queues validation and prevents release. Readiness should not flap because an optional lab is unavailable. Graceful shutdown stops accepting work, drains bounded requests, renews/releases leases safely and terminates after a deadline.

Use managed secrets with per-environment/service identities and rotation; protect production data from development/test roles. Deploy immutable images/build artifacts and versioned configuration after reproducible install/type/build tests. Run index/data migrations as reviewed jobs with backups and dry-run evidence; startup must not backfill or reconcile indexes on every API boot. A versioned create-only manifest job creates required collections/indexes and waits for completion, without dropping/replacing existing indexes or deleting duplicates. Preflight checks keys, uniqueness, collation/partial/sparse options and conflicts; incompatible definitions or duplicate data stop deployment for a reviewed resolution. Readiness verifies the required correctness-index manifest read-only and blocks affected writers if it is absent/mismatched. Existing `sync-indexes` is not this job; production `autoIndex` remains off. [Index creation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index/), [unique-index prerequisites](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/). Health responses disclose no secrets.

Connection budget: cap each process pool, transaction concurrency, provider sockets and worker classes. Calculate sum of configured per-process DB pools plus driver/monitoring/failover overhead against actual database limits. Autoscaling API replicas multiplies pools and can overload the DB; set scaling ceilings. Measure pool waits, event-loop delay, heap, CPU, DB latency/write conflicts, scanned/returned ratio, queue lag and provider outcomes before adding replicas.

## 14. Capacity model and 100 RPS verification

100 RPS means **100 aggregate incoming HTTP requests/second**, not 100 users, 100 per endpoint or 100 completed patient journeys. At 1 second average latency, roughly 100 requests are in flight; use actual endpoint latency and request distribution to size clients/pools. Provider traffic and file bytes are separate measurements. Proposed expanded profile below matches the existing performance plan.

| Category | Requests/s | Examples / prerequisites |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Catalogue/provider/stock discovery | 20 | Private item/tariff and public pharmacy/service discovery, price entitlement; cache-hit and miss cases |
| Patient/clinical reads | 15 | Authorized private/direct patient summary, timeline and report metadata, without requiring patient app login |
| Staff worklists/dashboard | 20 | Doctor appointments, direct/app lab orders, hospital stores and business/vendor worklists; trusted branch/location filters |
| Bookings and appointment changes | 10 | App/walk-in capacity holds and changes; synthetic available capacity |
| Sales/service billing and POS commands | 10 | Pharmacy checkout, private consultation/test invoices, counter sales and permitted fulfilment; source/tariff snapshots |
| Purchasing and stock/consumption commands | 10 | Receive, reserve/consume, waste, count and issue/receive transfer; pharmacy versus non-medicine item/UOM rules |
| Collection verification/receipts | 5 | Stubbed gateway verification and connected cash receipt recording |
| Inbound provider events | 5 | Authenticated events with deliberate replay in a separately tagged subcase |
| Follow-up/service updates | 5 | Task completion, lab transitions or vendor order updates |
| **Total** | **100** | Multi-request journeys must allocate each request within these rates |

At least 50 RPS of this proposed profile exercises private/direct operations, including successful writes, with some businesses unlisted. Run a separate marketplace-focused 100 RPS profile rather than silently adding them into 200 RPS. Lab API and panel flows must both be represented. Use the seeded dataset and 30-minute steady/two-hour soak gates in [PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md](PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md), including contention and failure cases; do not substitute a health endpoint or repeated409 responses.

Query budgets: bounded cursor pagination, deliberate projections, compound indexes and limits on date ranges/exports. Bulk import/report generation is asynchronous and bounded. Report offered and achieved cache-hit/miss ratio per workload category, with fixed warm/cold profiles and an explicit upper bound for the agreed acceptance profile. Do not tune cache ratio to hide transactional/uncached work. Public catalog caches may use short TTL/version invalidation; no private clinical response enters shared public cache. Displayed stock/availability can be a projection, but every sale/hold revalidates the authority. Do not cache permissions so long that staff revocation is ineffective.

API deadlines and provider timeouts are selected per operation from measured latency. Local transactional SLO excludes provider completion only when the endpoint clearly reports durable processing; report that distinction in results. Limit retries within an end-to-end budget, isolate provider concurrency and return explicit overload errors instead of unbounded queues. Call external providers outside local transactions; operational fallback never fabricates a paid booking or released result.

Use k6 or equivalent after install/build repair. In arrival-rate testing, iteration rate is not automatically request rate; report actual HTTP count, offered/started/completed/successful rates and dropped work. Capture application/config/test revisions, hardware, dataset, provider mode and integrity reconciliations. Full methodology and release thresholds remain canonical in the performance plan; no upstream project benchmark is evidence for this deployment.

## 15. Failure handling and observability

| Failure / race | Required behavior | Detection / recovery owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client times out after local commit | Same command key retrieves original authorized result | API/command metrics; backend |
| Capture after hold expiry | Preserve collection; controlled reallocation or refund/recovery | Payment reconciliation and oldest pending-compensation alert; finance/backend |
| Worker crashes after external effect | Replay original identity, lookup external result, avoid duplicate mutation | Lease expiry, delivery attempts and unknown-outcome worklist; integrations |
| Duplicate/stale lab events | Dedupe and preserve report version/state; reconcile gaps | Provider mapping/version metrics; lab operations |
| API and panel both try to act | Expected assignment mode/version fences old writer | Conflict audit and authorized handover; lab lead |
| DB unavailable/unknown commit | No false success; bounded retry/idempotent lookup; preserve external evidence | DB/pool/readiness alerts; DevOps/backend |
| Report/storage/scanner unavailable | Pending artifact, no public fallback or unverified release | Validation/backlog/link checks; documents/lab lead |
| External ERP/LIS unavailable | Pending operation or unavailable capability; no competing native stock writer | Adapter health/reconciliation; facility operations |
| Subscription delinquency | Apply agreed entitlements/grace; preserve data/export/urgent-care continuity under policy | Billing/support worklist; product/operations |
| Credential/revoked-staff event | Rotate/revoke, block sensitive access, audit scope and reissue integrations | Security alerts and incident runbook; security/DevOps |

Logs use request/correlation/operation/event/resource IDs and safe status codes; redact tokens, identifiers beyond need, medical content and raw signatures. Metrics use bounded cardinality rather than patient IDs. Clinical access and privileged changes have protected audit records with actor, purpose, scope, before/after references and outcome; regular business users cannot edit them. Retention and access are separate from application debug logs.

Initial alert proposals: urgent if capture/refund discrepancies appear, unauthorized access occurs, accepted writes cannot reconcile or durable acceptance fails; warn if normal-task p95 age exceeds 30 seconds or backlog grows across successive windows. Clinical urgent-result escalation deadlines are set by the clinical team, not the normal queue SLO. Dashboards separate local API latency, provider completion, money recovery, sample/report turnaround, restore status and store/capacity reconciliation. Each alert/runbook has an accountable human role and replay/correction steps.

Backups encrypt database and object versions with independently protected keys. Restore into an isolated environment and reconcile patient mappings, report hashes, invoice/journal/stock totals, in-flight holds and pending events. After restore, re-pull gateway payment/order/refund and lab-provider facts across an overlapping recovery window from the restore point, compare existing external IDs and captured versions, and queue mismatches without duplicate effects. Source systems may contain newer captures/reports than the backup. Backup success alone does not prove RPO/RTO. Export supports authorized business continuity without exposing another business or silently losing amendments/financial references.

### 15.1 Restore admission and authority freshness (AR-29)

Keep sensitive access, optional sends and irreversible mutations closed while restoring. Advance a recovery generation in a protected control plane outside the restored rollback domain and require all API/worker instances to observe it before admission. Invalidate pre-restore sessions/access grants and all outstanding OTP/setup/reset challenges; do not restore usable consumed challenges. A new token minted after restore is not proof that restored membership, consent, caregiver, contact or credential data is current. Recover post-backup revocation/consumption evidence from an independently recoverable journal or require approved independent re-verification before issuing fresh authority. If freshness cannot be established, keep that subject/scope blocked with an accountable assisted route. Resume sensitive deliveries only after current recipient/purpose/authority is established; regenerated jobs do not inherit stale grants. Select the concrete control-plane/evidence mechanism and failure policy before restore acceptance; no additional microservice or external product is chosen here.

### 15.2 Recoverability of irreversible effects (AR-30)

Classify each acknowledged effect by its recoverable evidence: gateway/provider facts, local cash receipt, dispensing/physical movement, manual refund, issued invoice and finalized clinical work. The generic proposed RPO <=15 minutes is not proof that acknowledged local effects inside that window are reconstructable. A provider cannot replay a cash collection or physical dispense it never saw, and an outbox in the same restored database is not independent recovery evidence. Before pilot, choose and rehearse per-effect recoverability/acknowledgement rules using proven PITR/independently durable receipt or journal evidence, or an approved stop-and-reconcile process with finance/pharmacy/clinical ownership.

During reconciliation fence affected accounts/lots/capacity/commands, retain unresolved operation identities/obligations, and do not infer fresh stock, unused refund budgets or unspent money from the old snapshot. Independent physical counts, receipts and source evidence may resolve exceptions under audit; missing evidence remains an explicit exception, not a successful restoration claim or a repeated irreversible effect. Replaying the original command ID cannot collect/dispense/refund again merely because its old idempotency row is absent. Measure data-loss/recovery outcomes separately for each effect class and test restore of post-backup revocations, consumed challenges, cash/dispense/manual-return effects and files. Resume only with named admission approval and independently verified balances/authority. No zero-loss or zero-RPO guarantee is asserted before those mechanisms are demonstrated.

## 16. Migration and compatibility rollout

1. **M0: foundation and existing-flow recovery.** Repair build/start and credential/OTP/access findings; add raw-body authenticated gateway webhook and independent reconciliation, reject bad client signatures without state mutation, accept collection only from captured evidence, reconcile before bounded hold release and route cancelled/deleted-resource payments to recovery. Stop fixed-name report overwrite, protect available report versions/partial labels and remove public clinical cache paths. Deliver the create-only correctness-index job/readiness gate and synthetic replica-set tests. These are live-path design blockers, not work deferred until M2/M4; no source fix is performed by this document.
2. **M1 and pre-M2 financial cutover.** Add business/patient/consent contracts and reviewed ownership mappings. Before any M2 business/wallet journal posting, classify legacy wallet/paid/refunded evidence and load reconciled customer wallet-liability and platform/business opening balances under the approved D1/D2 account map. Use a reviewed cutoff and bounded write freeze (or an equally proven single-writer watermark protocol): opening entries cover through the cutoff, later unique effects replay once, and activation occurs only after source balances/transactions and ledger totals reconcile. Unexplained differences block the new ledger rollout and enter a finance exception queue; do not post against uninitialized liabilities or invent old gateway refunds. No pharmacyId/corporateId mapping is assumed without validation.
3. **M2–M3: migrate vertical slices.** Put old booking/pharmacy/payment entry points behind new authorized operations. Backfill scoped IDs/snapshots through dry-run reports, with exception queues. Missing history remains unknown; do not fabricate consent, lot expiry, prices or payment facts.
4. **Reconcile and enforce.** Compare counts, quantities, patient/document references, invoice/receipt/journal balances and active holds. Add reviewed indexes/constraints after resolving duplicates. Shadow policy checks first, then enforce per business; no uncontrolled dual stock/payment writer.
5. **M4–M5: integrate labs and OPD.** Expand the M0 immutable-report bridge into native lab review and complete private-storage access. Migrate available bytes with checksum, provenance and `versionHistory: unknown` if prior versions were overwritten; do not manufacture historical reports. Financial legacy classification/opening balances already precede M2 under step 2; this phase does not defer them. Add panel and API contracts, hospital department context and business/vendor workspace. Retain accepted orders when publication/settings change.
6. **M6: controlled cutover.** Feature flags by business/module, canary synthetic journeys, rehearsed data/export/restore and useful 100 RPS gates; train staff and publish support/recovery ownership. Back up before cutover; record migration revision and checkpoints.

Use expand/backfill/verify/switch/contract. Schema additions remain compatible until old clients/workers are drained. Binary rollback is allowed only where schema/API versions remain compatible. If new financial/clinical effects occurred, stop writes, reconcile and forward-fix or execute a rehearsed data rollback with a defined loss/recovery window; blindly restoring yesterday's database can erase real collections and reports. Every data migration specifies resumability, dry-run, verification, rollback/forward plan and accountable operator.

# Shared business staff authority — initial implementation contract

12 November 2026. Draft for two independent nonauthor Spec and Standards reviews before source edits. Baseline authority sources are bound below at focus df8fd4ef00cb9d45d081ce760d15cef84a880c4e; unrelated later edits do not change these bindings. Root owns integration. This contract follows SYSTEM_DESIGN sections 4–6, the domain glossary and the delegated pharmacy policy. It introduces one reusable authority boundary for pharmacy and lab staff, not a new login, general RBAC engine, organization migration or clinical workflow.

## Outcome and exact initial slice

Implement one usable internal resolver that turns an authenticated individual plus a requested business/branch/capability into a current, narrowly scoped BusinessScope, or denies. Implement its persistence shapes, restricted read adapter and framework-free eligibility rules. Valid synthetic facts must produce the expected scope; missing/invalid facts must deny. The initial source slice exposes no HTTP route, grant/verification writer, bootstrap command, index migration, clinical command, protected-data reader or payment/stock effect. It does not silently enable existing routes or promote existing business/admin tokens.

New production files only:

| File under src1/modules/organizations | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| types/index.ts | Closed capability/purpose and record types; readonly authority facts, lookup and scope; narrow read-port interface. No Express/Mongoose/typedi dependency. |
| rules.ts | Pure validation/evaluation of supplied facts and server time, including all cross-record/proof/version checks below; no database, environment, configuration, provider or logger access. |
| model/index.ts | Four explicitly named Mongoose schemas/models below, with strict fields and index declarations; no startup index creation/synchronization or data seeding. |
| repository/index.ts | The sole Mongo authority adapter and the explicit narrow projection adapters for existing User and Pharmacy facts. No inheritance from unscoped BaseRepository; no arbitrary caller filter/update/model exposure. |
| services/index.ts | Constructor-injected read port; validate caller context, obtain current facts within the caller's transaction, invoke the one rule evaluator and mint/freeze the internal scope. No default permissive port or singleton environment switch. |

No root dependency/lock/build/start, existing auth/user/pharmacy/admin source or routes change. Source QA may contain exact diff/hashes and review records. Meaningful pure-rule/port tests may be added to a separately reviewed focused test entry; do not add a redundant lexical-test framework, copy production controllers or run application imports under this contract.

## Identity and scope

- Reuse existing personal User._id, authenticated by the existing signature-verifying middleware, with userType exactly user. The resolver takes only an internal authenticated-principal projection, not a body/header token decoder. Reload the User by exact ID; require stored userType=user and isActive=true. Missing/false/unknown state denies. User.isVerified/otpVerified and linkedPharmacyId never establish professional or staff authority.
- A pharmacy token identifies a business, not a person. Reject pharmacy/admin/hr/specialist tokens for this resolver, including an admin with self-edited permissions. An individual may have customer and staff roles, but each invocation explicitly uses purpose=staff; do not union patient/dependent/caregiver rights or infer consent.
- Canonical organizationId is a new organization record ID. Initial mapping kind is pharmacy or lab; legacy business IDs remain separate references. Do not copy pharmacyId/corporateId into organizationId or invent an organization for an API provider. Branch IDs are explicit embedded organization branches; no implicit branch, wildcard, omitted branch or all-branches capability.
- Input contains exactly requested organizationId, branchId and one supported capability. Initial closed capabilities are pharmacy.prescription.review and lab.report.release. The first requires profession=pharmacist; the second requires profession=lab_signatory. A capability grants only the named action in this scope, never finance, catalogue, stock quality, exports, contact changes or professional verification.
- All IDs must be canonical lowercase 24-hex strings, with no coercion from objects, whitespace or numbers. Versions are positive safe integers; digests are lowercase 64-hex SHA-256. Arrays are bounded (at most 100 branches/grants), have unique keys and no unknown capability/branch/profession values. Reject malformed stored records as well as malformed input; Mongoose casting is not the validator.

The initial real business adapter supports only pharmacy. It reloads exact Pharmacy._id from the canonical organization mapping and requires isActive=true, isVerified=true and absent archivedAt. It checks that the protected mapping's source-field fingerprint still matches the current license number/document reference; business verification alone is insufficient. A changed or absent fingerprint denies even if the legacy verified flag remains true. The fingerprint detects changed fields, not overwritten remote URL bytes; immutable verification evidence is separately required. Lab always denies with AUTHORITY_MAPPING_UNAVAILABLE until its actual canonical business/branch adapter is separately contracted and reviewed. Lab types and capability use the same resolver; no fake lab ID or permissive placeholder adapter.

## Minimal persisted authority records

Use these four collections only. They contain authority/provenance references, not patient records, prescription/report content, credentials, document URLs or authentication secrets. IDs are immutable; createdAt/updatedAt are UTC. No public generic CRUD or direct model access outside the approved adapter. Every current record has schemaVersion=1 and positive revision, incremented by future protected writers; unknown versions deny.

| Collection | Required fields and invariant |
| --- | --- |
| business_authority_organizations | _id, kind, sourceBusinessId, state=active/suspended/revoked, revision, sourceFingerprint, mappingDecisionId, bounded branches[{branchId,state,revision}]. Exactly one organization per kind+sourceBusinessId, each branch belongs to that organization. No source/mapping/branch replacement through a profile update. |
| business_staff_memberships | _id, organizationId, actorId, state=active/suspended/revoked, revision, validFrom, expiresAt, and bounded grants[{branchId,capability,grantDecisionId}]. Exactly one current membership per organization+actor, retaining revoked rows. A grant is branch-specific and names a protected decision; capability arrays alone are not provenance. |
| business_professional_eligibility | _id, organizationId, actorId, profession, state=verified/suspended/revoked, revision, validFrom, expiresAt, verificationDecisionId, evidenceVersionId and evidenceSha256. One current record per organization+actor+profession. This is current verified eligibility, not a copied user/business flag; the referenced professional decision supplies the permitted branch/capability scope. History is retained in immutable decision records. |
| business_authority_decisions | _id, organizationId, operationId, decisionKind=business_mapped/membership_granted/professional_verified, subjectActorId where relevant, decidingActorId, decidedAt, authorityGeneration, schemaVersion=1, payloadSha256, exact payload and immutable evidence references. No update/delete methods. Payloads bind the exact relevant organization/source fingerprint, branch/grant, subject, record revision, profession and credential evidence versions/validity. Unknown kinds or mismatches deny. |

The resolver checks mapping, grant and professional decisions against the current records, not just that a decision ID exists. A grant/verification decidingActorId must differ from its subjectActorId. Membership-grant and professional-verification are distinct decision kinds; neither implies the other. A decision records the authority and evidence at decision time; a later verifier-role change does not silently rewrite history. Revoking current eligibility/membership or invalidating evidence blocks current use.

Decision authenticity originates in the separately protected grant/bootstrap path, not a client-supplied document or database label. A read-only readiness port supplies the accepted authorityGeneration and verified index/provenance readiness from trusted composition; it is not request input, an environment boolean or an editable Admin field. It defaults closed. All three decisions must match that accepted generation. Initial source supplies no way to activate it or fabricate records. No existing app/admin/profile writer may mint these records. Threats from privileged database tampering and restore rollback require the existing security/restore controls; schema immutability alone is not advertised as cryptographic or operational authenticity.

Use a fixed schema-versioned array serialization for each decision kind before SHA-256: explicit ordered field names/values, canonical IDs, integer revisions/epoch-millisecond times, sorted unique branch/capability entries and exact evidence digests. Do not hash arbitrary object iteration order, omit absent-vs-null distinctions or accept a submitted digest without recomputing it. The exact serialization vectors form part of the implementation review. Stored payload and recomputed digest must match the referenced current record snapshot. No remote evidence fetch occurs during resolution.

## Scoped reads and current-fact consistency

The read port exposes only readiness(), loadFacts(lookup, transaction, now) and no generic query, write or list operation. lookup contains the authenticated actorId plus exact organizationId, branchId and capability. The resolver validates these before any persistence access. Each production call requires an explicit caller-owned ClientSession in an active snapshot transaction; no session-less fallback, nested transaction, unrelated session, cache, provider call or automatic retry. Missing/invalid session/readiness denies before authority reads. The adapter never starts/commits/ends the caller's transaction. It projects only required authority fields and returns plain immutable data to rules.

Exact Mongo query restrictions:

1. User: {_id: actorId, userType: 'user', isActive: true}; project ID/type/active only. This is an individual identity lookup, not a private patient/profile fetch.
2. Organization: {_id: organizationId, state: 'active', branches: {$elemMatch: {branchId, state: 'active'}}}; require exactly one matching embedded branch. A legacy business ID is read only after this mapping succeeds.
3. Pharmacy business: {_id: sourceBusinessId, isActive: true, isVerified: true, archivedAt: {$exists: false}}; project only ID/status and fingerprint source fields. Any present archivedAt, even malformed/null, denies under this strict new boundary. Unsupported kind denies before querying another business collection.
4. Membership: {organizationId, actorId, state: 'active', validFrom: {$lte: now}, expiresAt: {$gt: now}, grants: {$elemMatch: {branchId, capability}}}. Enforce one current row and one matching grant; ambiguity denies.
5. Professional eligibility: {organizationId, actorId, profession: requiredProfession, state: 'verified', validFrom: {$lte: now}, expiresAt: {$gt: now}}. Enforce one row and matching branch/capability in the verification decision.
6. Each decision: {_id: referencedDecisionId, organizationId, decisionKind: expectedKind, authorityGeneration: acceptedGeneration}; grant and professional decisions additionally require subjectActorId=actorId. Compare the full binding/digest in rules. Do not merge an externally supplied filter or use $or to relax these predicates.

Authority construction is the explicitly narrow bootstrap query boundary preceding a verified BusinessScope; it may inspect only the requesting person's authority in the exact requested organization. It is not a generic exception allowing other modules to read unscoped business or patient records. No list/count/aggregate/export/file/job surface is added in this slice. Future private business repositories must require the minted scope and compose restrictive ownership/branch predicates on every operation.

Capture one finite server time from an injected trusted clock per resolution, never a request timestamp; pass that exact value to loadFacts and rules. Require validFrom <= now < expiresAt for membership and professional eligibility, with finite dates and valid intervals. Require mapping/grant/verification decisions not in the future. Scope expiresAt is the earlier membership/eligibility expiry. Every invocation reloads facts in its transaction; no JWT role cache or cross-request reuse. Database errors, missing/duplicate rows, malformed facts, unknown evidence and readiness failure reject; no catch returns an allow result.

A successful result is a deeply frozen, internally minted BusinessScope containing actorId, organizationId, exactly one branchId, purpose=staff, capability, kind/sourceBusinessId, organization/branch/membership/eligibility revisions, exact decision/evidence references, checkedAt and expiresAt. Minting uses a module-private runtime identity check (for example, a WeakSet) rather than trusting a caller-shaped object or TypeScript brand alone. Do not include patient details, license contents, bearer tokens or unnecessary profile data. This is a reusable internal authority result, not a new session/JWT or proof of patient consent.

## Revocation, sensitive commands and audit boundary

The initial resolver establishes eligibility at its transaction snapshot. It does not promise that a later mutation or delivery is safe merely because a scope object exists. No sensitive command is activated in this slice. Before a prescription/report/financial/stock writer consumes this interface, its separate contract must resolve/revalidate in the command transaction, compare current subject/resource/document versions and perform a genuine shared write/CAS fence against concurrent authority revocation. Reading the same old snapshot twice is insufficient. Every grant/revoke and subject/business disable path participating in that contract must conflict on the same fences; until that is implemented and race-tested, sensitive command activation stays closed. Delayed jobs must resolve current authority afresh and preserve the initiator; a captured scope is not a durable grant.

Protected decision interfaces are data contracts here, not an approval/rejection endpoint. A future clinical writer binds the individual, scope and authority revisions to immutable patient/document/item/order versions, reason and decision time. It must distinguish imported/unverified evidence from finalized clinical authorship and enforce current patient/purpose authorization separately. This contract makes no prescription decision and releases no report. Finance/recovery permissions and stock-quality release require their own closed capabilities and contracts; do not reuse pharmacy.prescription.review for them.

No audit sink is invented or falsely claimed operational in this slice. The resolver returns a redacted decision reference set for the future protected command audit. It must not log raw tokens, credential documents, patient data or arbitrary record bodies. Public adapters added later must map missing authentication to 401, denied/hidden authority to one uniform 403 AUTHORITY_DENIED without tenant-existence details, and temporary readiness/mapping infrastructure failure to a generic unavailable response. Internally preserve typed denial categories for focused checks. An existing route is never silently changed by this work.

## Bootstrap, activation and indexes

The initial slice has no provisioning escape hatch. The readiness port defaults closed, records are not auto-created on login, and no existing admin/business/self-profile capability is trusted. A later independently reviewed local protected bootstrap/grant command must establish the first real organization mapping and branch, independently verify the individual and professional evidence, preserve a protected operation/evidence record, prove the issuer's authority without circular self-granting, and install/verify the required indexes through the create-only readiness process. It must distinguish developer-created synthetic fixtures from real grants and must not derive production authority from test data. Real professional verification and individual clinical decisions remain human workflow facts; no additional product-policy naming question is needed to develop this boundary.

Declared correctness indexes:

- Organization unique {kind:1, sourceBusinessId:1}.
- Membership unique {organizationId:1, actorId:1}, across every state; revoked rows are not deleted to permit a second conflicting current membership.
- Eligibility unique {organizationId:1, actorId:1, profession:1}, across every state.
- Decision unique {organizationId:1, operationId:1}; same operation with a different payload is a conflict, not a new decision. _id uniqueness also applies.

Do not rely on a schema declaration as proof of installed uniqueness. Readiness must verify exact keys/options, conflict-free data and supported transaction topology before real activation; no destructive syncIndexes/drop or background migration is admitted. Branch/grant uniqueness is explicit validation and future write-CAS responsibility, not a purported Mongo multikey uniqueness guarantee. No live records or users are provisioned by this contract.

| paymentStatus | Exact stored pending,paid,cancelled,refunded, otherwise unknown. Informational legacy label only, not verified capture/refund/receipt/budget proof. No amounts/units are exposed or converted. |
| providerReferenceRecorded | true for a nonblank stored externalBookingId string of at most512 UTF-16 units; false for missing/null or an empty/whitespace-only string of at most512 units; null for any other malformed/overlong value, including an overlong whitespace-only string. ## Closed durable record, idempotency and money truth

Use optional embedded recoveryRequest with default undefined, strict closed sub-schema, _id:false, no legacy backfill/default request. One physical order document holds at most one request; no array, separate upsert collection or custom uniqueness index is needed. Shape:

- schemaVersion:1; operationKind:customer_recovery_request.
- operationId: exact server-derived pharmacy-recovery-request:v1:<canonicalOrderId>. It is an operation identity, not an authorization token or globally readable lookup key.
- requestingCustomerId: the validated owned account; orderId: canonical actual order ID; status:reconciliation_required only.
- requestedAt: actual server Date. No body/paidDate input; it means request record time only.
- observation: closed own fields orderStatusLabel and paymentStatusLabel (recognized existing labels or unknown), paymentRecordId (canonical24hex string or null), paymentRecordReferenceState:recorded|missing|malformed. A reference's presence proves no capture, amount, ownership or refund. Retain malformed/missing distinction without retaining arbitrary raw data.
- amountMinor:null; currency:null; instrument:unknown; destinationPolicy:original_instrument. Null is unknown, never zero or a validated debt/refund promise. No numeric arithmetic or local paid-label inference occurs.
- payloadSha256 and observationSha256: lowercase64hex digests over separate fixed schema-versioned ordered arrays. Request payload binds operation kind/version/order/customer; observation digest binds exact stored first observation and requestedAt epoch. Freeze exact serialization vectors in implementation review. Digests detect inconsistent data, not protected provenance against a privileged database rewrite.

The successful POST stores only this record and the ordinary order updatedAt maintained by the existing timestamps mechanism. It never changes order.status/paymentStatus/items, payment records, currency, reservation/stock/quality, coupon counts, wallet/ledger balances or provider state. No notification/subscription/audit-sink/queue/worker is invoked. A request is an obligation to reconcile facts and determine whether money is owed; it is not an executable refund intent or proof that custody was retained.

First creation uses a scoped same-session findOneAndUpdate with actual _id/customerId, scalar-type checks and recoveryRequest:{$exists:false}; upsert:false, runValidators:true, return new, fixed projection, maxTimeMS2000. Repository exposes only mandatory canonical order/customer arguments and a caller-owned session; never optional scope or FilterQuery/options from the request. It validates returned ownership/identity and the closed stored record/digests before returning a DTO. Malformed required stored identity/record produces503 PHARMACY_RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE / Pharmacy recovery is unavailable; no repair or raw error echo.

Exact replay returns the same stored request/observation/time, not a new operation or refreshed observation. Validate stored operation/order/customer/digests before returning; never overwrite/reopen a malformed, conflicting or unknown-version record. If the insert CAS misses, one further scoped read may identify the committed same request; missing/changed ownership404, malformed/conflicting record503. No alternate ID/key, ownerless lookup, blind update, catch-as-success or free-running application retry. An uncertain commit must remain an error until the same deterministic operation is read/reconciled; no newly generated key.

The command transaction must use the same actual Mongoose client/session for scoped read and marker write, snapshot readConcern and one existing driver withTransaction boundary, no nested session/provider action. Its normal driver transaction/commit retries are not advertised as zero retries; every re-executed callback uses the same deterministic operation identity and no external effect. A transaction abort leaves no marker. Concurrent requests have one committed first observation; losers may return that exact committed request after a bounded scoped read or surface the driver's failure. No duplicate success is inferred from duplicate-key/write-conflict errors alone. This is marker idempotency, not money/stock exactly-once proof.

# Delegated prescription and recovery policy decisions

12 November 2026. The owner answered the clinical/finance decision question: “you cna decide yourself”. Root accepts responsibility for selecting product and technical policy. These are the selected development defaults; exact implementation contracts and independent reviews still precede code. This delegation does not make an AI a pharmacist, verify a professional, approve a real prescription, deploy code or authorize real money/stock actions. Qualified human decisions on individual cases remain part of the implemented workflow.

## Selected operating policy

| Boundary | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Reviewer identity | Use an individual authenticated person, not a shared pharmacy business login. Require current active account, explicit current business/branch review capability and independently verified professional eligibility. OTP verification, customer linkage, business verification and administrator status alone confer no clinical-review authority. |
| Grant/verification authority | Separate membership/capability grants, credential verification and clinical review. No user may verify themselves or gain authority through a profile field. Existing self-editable Admin.permissions is not a trusted capability registry. Provision protected grants through separately reviewed authority/bootstrap controls; absent grants fail closed. |
| Clinical decision | A verified authorized pharmacist approves/rejects the actual prescription. The application and AI do not decide medical validity. Require protected reviewer identity/time/reason/evidence references; bind the decision to immutable document, patient and order-item versions. Reject mismatched, stale, revoked or unknown evidence. Attachment alone never approves dispensing. |
| Progress | Block packed, ready-for-pickup, dispatch and completion unless the required current review is eligible. Keep payment requirements separate. A new order may remain awaiting review, with truthful customer status and a controlled cancellation path; never auto-approve or relabel it not_required to unblock it. |
| Patient/payer | Keep the clinical patient distinct from login, payer, pharmacy customer link and dependent-account ownership. No phone/name merge or assumed guardian consent. Verification and purpose-bound representation are explicit dependencies of clinical enablement. |
| Before handover | Cancellation must establish controlled custody/no handover, claim the transition once, release only the exact live reservation and durably create any money-return obligation. A stock release is not a financial refund. |
| After dispatch/handover | Use a separate return/failed-delivery/exception workflow. Do not put physically dispatched or returned goods directly into saleable stock. Inspection/quality disposition and financial settlement are separate recorded decisions. |
| Legacy ready/out orders | Keep an accountable recovery case/worklist. Reconcile actual custody, reservation and payment facts per order. No blanket completion, database backfill, deletion, forced cancellation or assumed refund. Unknown facts remain blocked for an authorized operator. |
| Funds proof | Treat authorization, capture, settlement, wallet debit, cash collection and refund as distinct facts. The existing paid/refunded labels are not sufficient proof. Bind server-side resource, payer, amount, currency and provider references; ignore client-selected fulfillment context. |
| Refund destination | Return each verified funded component to its original instrument by default. Do not silently replace a gateway refund with application wallet credit. An alternate destination requires a separately recorded, explicit customer choice and verified authority. |
| Amount/budget | Use explicit currency and integer minor units in new intents, with reviewed conversions at legacy rupee boundaries. Reserve outstanding refund budget transactionally against verified capture/debit facts. No rounding, omitted amount, duplicate payout or provider-fee deduction is used to repair uncertain records. |
| Completion/retry | Persist one operation identity and payload hash before effects. Mark refunded only after a matching confirmed financial effect. Pending, failed and unknown are not completed. Reconcile ambiguous provider outcomes; do not generate a new operation key or blindly repeat an unproved effect. |
| Financial/operations roles | Explicit current finance/recovery and pharmacy-operations capabilities authorize their own decisions. Clinical approval does not grant refund authority, and financial authority does not approve a prescription or stock quality. All privileged decisions use protected audit references. |

Existing source requires repair before it can implement this policy: no individual pharmacist membership/credential system exists; authorized gateway payments are currently accepted as paid; pharmacy timeout recovery credits an application wallet instead of a gateway refund; duplicate ledger errors can be mistaken for completed refunds. See [the source baseline](PHARMACY_AUTHORITY_RECOVERY_BASELINE.md). Do not reuse these labels or helpers as trusted proof without their separate hardening contracts.

## Provider facts checked for the policy

Razorpay's payment fetch schema distinguishes authorized/captured states and exposes captured flag, order reference, currency, payment amount and refunded amount in currency subunits. A local paid flag or a valid callback signature alone does not establish the selected application's capture invariant. [Payment API](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/payments/fetch-with-id/), [integration capture guidance](https://razorpay.com/docs/server-integration/python/test-app/).

The Normal Refund API requires eligible captured funds, positive integer subunits and supported payment methods; an omitted amount can request the full refund. Its receipt detects reuse on the same payment. Our adapter must reconcile the existing operation on duplicates/uncertain responses, not assume a universal idempotency header.   - exact key shapes, canonical lowercase IDs, safe-integer revisions and time bounds;
  - mapping, grant and verification payloads against the current records (rules ~L193-227);
  - deciding actor != subject, with unique decision IDs and operation IDs;

  - scope expiresAt = min(membership, eligibility).

Models use autoIndex/autoCreate false and strict throw, register only through the adapter, and conflicting pre-registration gives NOT_READY. There is no route, writer or wiring.

Findings (non-blocking):
- F1-1 LOW latent (repository L85-91; rules ~L198).
  - Trigger: lab requests return AUTHORITY_DENIED when the org is missing or not a lab. They return AUTHORITY_MAPPING_UNAVAILABLE only after an active lab org with an active branch matched, for any active ordinary user.

  - Minimum fix before any public adapter: deny `lab.report.release` with MAPPING_UNAVAILABLE before the User read, or collapse it into the uniform 403.
  - Check: a lab capability against a missing org, a pharmacy org and an active lab org gives one identical category with zero org reads.
- F1-2 LOW design (rules ~L213-215; model L29 with immutable canonicalId L5).
  - Trigger: the grant decision binds membershipRevision and the full grants snapshot, while each grant's `grantDecisionId` is immutable.
  - Consequence: any membership revision, such as adding a second branch grant, invalidates every older grant decision. Those grants deny until they are re-pointed. This fails closed and matches the contract.
  - Fix: the future writer contract must define re-issue/re-point semantics and race-test them.

  - Trigger: `isBusinessScope` checks the brand only, not expiry or revocation.
  - Fix: future consumers must check `expiresAt` against a trusted clock and re-resolve inside the command transaction with a real write fence. A consumer API that takes `now` and refuses expired scopes is recommended.

## R8-1 Customer lab progress: APPROVE_SOURCE_ONLY

Verified:

- **Route** (externalBookings/routes L138-142): GET `/diagnostics/bookings/:id/progress` with `catchAsync` only.
  - It sits behind the central `authenticate` mount (src1/routes/index.ts L101).
  - No earlier GET matches this path, and the route shadows no existing route.
  - No Joi schema, query or body reaches the service.
- **Controller** (L586-590): forwards only `req.user` and `req.params.id`, sets `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, returns `{success:true,data}` and logs nothing.
- **Service** (L2466-2475):
  - A non-object or array actor gets 401.
  - `userType !== 'user'` gets 403 "Individual customer access is required".
  - It then delegates `(id, principal._id)` and makes no provider, report, payment or wallet call.
- **Repository** (L23-71):
  - A non-lowercase-24-hex scope gets 403 before the ID check; a bad ID gets 400; both happen before any query is built.
  - It runs one `findOne` on an ObjectId `_id`, the literal `userId` and the literal `DIAGNOSTICS`, with `$expr` guards requiring both `userId` and `providerType` to be scalar strings.
  - The read uses a 10-field select with `maxTimeMS(2000).lean()`.
  - Missing, foreign and non-diagnostics bookings all get the same 404.
  - After the read (L44-49), it returns 503 for a non-ObjectId `_id`, a hex mismatch, or an owner or kind mismatch.
- **DTO:** exactly 11 constructed fields, with the contracted encodings.
  - `integration` is a closed set.
  - `bookingDateRaw` must match `^[0-9]{8}$`; `bookingTimeRaw` must be 1-32 characters.
  - `bookingStatus` is the closed 9-status vocabulary including `phlebo_assigned`; `paymentStatus` uses the closed labels.
  - `providerReferenceRecorded` is false for undefined or null; for a string of at most 512 characters it reports whether the string is non-blank; it is null otherwise, so an overlong whitespace string gives null.
  - `sampleState` and `reportReleaseState` are always `unknown`, and `source` is `local_record`.
  - `lastRecordedAt` is set only for a real Date with a safe epoch from 0 to 8.64e15 (at most 27 ISO characters).
  - No external ID, URL, patient field or amount is returned.
- **Scope of change:** the candidate diff is purely additive (imports plus new methods); legacy methods and routes are preserved.

Findings:

- **R8-F1-1 INFO (runtime).** The scalar-owner guard depends on Mongoose 6.13.8 passing a top-level `$expr` through query casting under the default `strictQuery`. The `instanceof Types.ObjectId` check depends on there being a single bson copy. Both fail closed here:
  - if `$expr` were dropped, an array owner would pass the query but hit the 503 at L44-49;
  - with a duplicate bson copy, every hit becomes a 503.

  Checks: an array `userId` containing the caller must give 503 or 404, never 200; a clean owned record must give 200.
- **R8-F1-2 LOW (compatibility).** Both ID and scope must be lowercase hex (repository L24 and L27). Sibling external routes accept any trimmed string and cast it case-insensitively.
  - Trigger: a client sends an uppercase ObjectId.
  - Consequence: 400, a client-visible inconsistency only.
  - Fix: either document the client contract, or accept `[0-9a-fA-F]{24}` and canonicalize it for the query only.

Limits (unchanged): stored status labels remain untrusted, and `report_delivered` does not mean release. HTTP, Joi, driver, response-byte and no-provider behaviour are NOT_RUN.

## R8-2 Customer pharmacy recovery intake: APPROVE_SOURCE_ONLY

Verified:

- **Routes** (L35-43): POST and GET `/:id/recovery-request`, with no guard or Joi, placed before `/:id` (L52). Authentication comes from the central mount.
- **Controller** (L27-37): forwards `req.user` and `req.params.id`, sets private/no-store, and returns 200 `{success,data}`.
- **Service `customerRecovery`** (~L773-810):
  - Checks run in this order: non-object actor 401; non-user 403; non-canonical signed `_id` 403; non-canonical order ID 400. All happen before `startSession`.
  - It opens one default-connection session and runs one `withTransaction` with readConcern `snapshot`.
  - `candidate`, `completed` and `transaction` are reset on every attempt, so a stale result from an earlier aborted attempt cannot be returned.
  - After a normal return it requires: `completed` set, a defined candidate, the same Transaction object, and `state === 'TRANSACTION_COMMITTED'`; anything else gives 503.
  - `endSession` runs in `finally`. The code correctly does not rely on the return value of driver 4 `withTransaction`.
- **Repository:**
  - `assertRecoverySession` (~L69-76) requires `instanceof mongo.ClientSession`, `client === PharmacyOrderModel.db.getClient()`, `inTransaction()`, the `snapshot` level, and an unchanged Transaction identity around every read and write.
  - `readCustomerRecoveryOrder` (~L78-93):
    - Scope 403, then ID 400.
    - One `findOne` on an ObjectId `_id` and ObjectId `customerId` with `$expr` objectId type guards, a 7-field projection, the session, `maxTimeMS` 2000 and `lean`.
    - Missing, foreign and wholesale (no `customerId`) orders get 404.
    - It returns 503 unless `_id`, `customerId` and `pharmacyId` are all ObjectIds that match.
- **Null versus absent marker:**
  - GET returns `null` only when the `recoveryRequest` key is absent (`hasOwnProperty`); a stored `null` goes to `recoveryReceipt(null)` and gets 503.
  - On POST, a present null or malformed marker gets 503 before the CAS, and `{$exists:false}` can never match a null marker. Malformed records are therefore never overwritten or repaired.
- **CAS** (~L120-124):
  - The filter repeats the same owner and type predicate and adds `recoveryRequest:{$exists:false}`.
  - The update is a `$set` of a newly built closed record only, with `upsert:false`, `runValidators:true`, a fixed projection and `maxTimeMS` 2000.
  - Afterwards it checks identity again and re-validates the receipt.
  - On a miss it does one scoped re-read in the same snapshot session; an absent marker then gives 503. It never uses an alternate key or an ownerless read.
- **Record** (`recoveryReceipt` ~L39-61, plus the model):
  - Exact own-data-key shapes for the record and the observation.
  - A deterministic operationId and an order/customer binding.
  - Closed labels, with the reference state consistent with the stored ID.
  - Amount and currency null, instrument `unknown`, destination `original_instrument`, and a safe epoch.
  - Payload and observation digests recomputed over fixed arrays. Both array layouts match the declared serializations in `SERIALIZATION_VECTORS.json` as text; I did not compute the hashes.
  - The model subschemas use `_id:false`, `strict:'throw'` and `default: undefined`, with no backfill.
- **DTO:** exactly 7 fields, with no customer ID, payment reference or gateway data.
- **Effects:** the new methods make no cancel, stock, payment, wallet, provider or queue call. Existing writers are byte-unchanged.

Findings:

- **R8-F2-1 MEDIUM (contract-design composition across R8-2, R8-6 and an unchanged writer).**
  - **Where:**
    - `pharmacyOrders/services` `update()` ~L881-897: `customerId` is an allowed "financial" edit while `status==='placed' && paymentStatus==='pending' && !paymentTransactionId`.
    - ~L985-990: `updatePayload.customerId = nextCustomerId`.
    - ~L1065: the final write uses only `{ _id: id }`, with no marker or owner predicate.
    - `recoveryReceipt` ~L45-46 binds `requestingCustomerId === customerId`.
    - The worklist validates each row against the row's current `customerId` (repository ~L189-205, call at L194).
  - **Trigger:** customer A files a request on A's own placed, non-Rx COD or in-store order (no payment transaction). The owning pharmacy then PUTs `customerId: B`, which the R7 commerce gate allows for non-Rx orders. Joi strips nothing relevant, so the marker is preserved but no longer consistent with the order.
  - **Consequences:**
    - (a) A now gets 404. That is correct authorization, but A loses the durable receipt.
    - (b) B gets 503 on GET and POST permanently, so B can never file a request for that order.
    - (c) Every worklist page containing that order returns a whole-page 503, hiding up to 49 valid requests. Because ordering is by `_id`, this never clears. No repair path exists.
  - **Assessment:** this is not a source deviation. Both contracts mandate a fail-closed 503 and byte-preserve the existing writers. It is still a reachable dead end caused by a legitimate existing command.
  - **Minimum fix (contract amendment, then source):** in `update()`, refuse any party change (customerId or buyerPharmacyId) when `order.recoveryRequest` exists (409). Also add `customerId: order.customerId` to the final write filter whenever the party changes, so the intake race is fenced. The alternative is an explicitly recorded reconciliation disposition.
  - **Checks:**
    - Record the current behaviour as evidence: a marker followed by reassignment gives A 404, B 503 and a page-wide 503.
    - With the fix, the reassignment gets 409.
    - Concurrent intake against reassignment.
    - Worklist pages that do not contain the order stay 200.
- **R8-F2-2 INFO (runtime).** Under snapshot isolation, a concurrent first writer normally surfaces as a WriteConflict (TransientTransactionError). The driver then re-runs the callback, and the loser takes the replay branch. The CAS-miss re-read branch is therefore mostly defensive.
  - Replay correctness depends on driver retry within its 120 s window.
  - An `UnknownTransactionCommitResult` that exhausts its retries propagates as 500 while the marker may already be committed; a client retry then replays it.

  Checks: two concurrent POSTs produce one marker, and either both responses are 200 with identical receipts or one surfaces a driver error. A forced unknown commit followed by a retry must replay the stored receipt.
- **Compatibility:** the same lowercase-only ID rule as R8-F1-2 applies here, whereas the module's `idParamSchema` accepts `[0-9a-fA-F]`.

## R8-3 Generic booking write boundary: APPROVE_SOURCE_ONLY

Verified:

- **Controller:** `resolveGenericBookingWriteScope` (L62-74) is the first statement of `update` (L378-379) and `delete` (L393-394).
  - The unchanged resolver runs first: 401 for a malformed actor, and 403 for a foreign owner hint from an exact user.
  - The unchanged HR 403 follows.
  - Any role other than exact `user` or `admin`, including padded or case variants, then gets 403 "Access to this booking resource is not permitted", before any service call.
  - A customer PUT still dispatches once to `updateCustomerNotes`, which is byte-unchanged. An admin keeps the shared `update` with the optional query owner, including when it is omitted.
- **Repository `deleteByIdAndUserId`** (L18-40):
  - A non-string or blank owner gets 401; a non-24-hex ID gets 400.
  - It then runs one `deleteOne({_id, userId:{$eq}, $expr:{$type of '$userId' is 'string'}})`.
  - It returns true only for `acknowledged===true && deletedCount===1`. Errors propagate, and there is no fallback.
- **Service `delete`** (~L1699-1734):
  - A supplied but invalid scope gets 401 before `getById`.
  - The pre-read and the reminder, Meet and slot sequence are byte-identical.
  - An omitted scope keeps the legacy unscoped `delete`. A supplied scope uses the scoped method, and `false` gives 409 BOOKING_DELETE_CONFLICT with no retry, re-read or fallback.
- **Specialist path:** specialist `updateAppointmentStatus` calls the shared `update`, which is untouched. The new guard lives only in the controller.

Findings: none introduced. These contracted residuals remain:

- Effects that run before a final 409 are not rolled back.
- A dirty array owner can pass the pre-read `getById` and trigger effects before the scalar final guard denies.
- A 12-character direct-call ID can match in `getById` and then get 400 after effects have run.
- An admin delete with omitted scope is unscoped and ignores the result.
- A customer can still hard-delete an own booking in any status (R4 B-C3).

- **R8-F3-1 INFO (runtime).** This has the same `$expr` dependency as R8-F1-1, but with no post-read fallback. If Mongoose ever stripped a top-level `$expr`, `{userId:{$eq}}` would match a dirty array containing the owner, and the booking would be deleted.

  Checks: dirty array, number, null and missing owners must give `deletedCount` 0 and 409; an exact scalar owner gives 200.

Baseline `dbe1cc2d972876876c422cf7af1b194037542575`, focus `/Users/shubham/Desktop/SwasthaDisha/SwasthaDisha-worktrees/customer-pharmacy-lab`. Two actual independent NONAUTHOR contract decisions precede source assignment; two fresh exact source decisions follow. Root selects technical/product details; business/user acceptance is unproved. ## Original scope and actual reuse finding

CAPABILITY_MATRIX B06 explicitly records supplier/PO/GRN/vendor-invoice chain Missing; ROADMAP U2 requires supplier accounts → purchase order → GRN → supplier invoice and purchase returns. BUSINESS_OPERATIONS pharmacy rows require supplier/purchase/receive; its proposed procurement boundary owns those references. SYSTEM_DESIGN receive-purchase boundary separates receipt/stock effects from supplier payment/account export.

Graph-first Supplier/PurchaseOrder/GRN search returned no nodes; known index identifies originalbfb608e. Current module-path and supplier/vendor/purchase-order/GRN literal checks found no supplier master/model/service. Vendor hits belong to Healthians/coupon targeting, not procurement. Existing inventory purchasePrice and purchase adjustment reason are not supplier accounts or receipt provenance. Do not repurpose pharmacyCustomers (patient-linked records), global Pharmacy profiles, inventory adjustments or a provider vendor ID.

Select a useful prerequisite only: the owning pharmacy's local supplier contact/reference metadata, with create/list/versioned-edit/archive. It is not a verified supplier legal identity, KYC/licence/GST status, buying eligibility, trade credit, payable, invoice, GRN or stock movement. No clinical qualification, funding or provider fact is needed for contact storage. Actual purchasing/receiving remains separately contracted; B06 stays incomplete.

## Concrete API and source boundary

Propose one narrow `pharmacySuppliers` module (types/model/repository/services/controller/routes/validation index.ts) plus one authenticated central mount `/api/v1/pharmacy-suppliers`; no generic ERP/framework or duplicate organization registry. This is the existing pharmacy-owned M0 adapter for future procurement references, explicitly not an activated organization/branch/staff BusinessScope. Later procurement must reference this stable local ID and separately verify the actual counterparty; no phone/email/name-based automatic organization merge or ownership inference.

All four routes use existing authenticate then requireOperationalPharmacy, preserving exact role/active/verified/archive errors and no admin bypass. Controller forwards only guard-resolved pharmacyId and signed actor `_id`, never body/query owner fallback. Direct service/repository methods require primitive lowercase24hex pharmacy scope; writes additionally require canonical signed actor ID. Invalid required scope gives403 FORBIDDEN / Access denied before supplier access. Canonical actor IDs record signed-subject provenance, not an individually qualified pharmacist. Existing guard fallback/token freshness and unwired staff-membership limitations remain explicit.
